title: Bayesian network predicts low or failed fertilization in IVF and ICSI cycles
summary: A Bayesian network learned from 106,640 fresh IVF/ICSI cycles at one Chinese centre (4,339 low fertilization rate and 5,199 total fertilization failure cases) used 18 of 24 predictors; infertility type, ART method and number of retrieved oocytes directly influenced the probabilities. With tenfold cross-validation, accuracy was 91.7%, and AUC was 0.779 (95% CI 0.766 to 0.791) for total failure versus controls and 0.807 (0.790 to 0.824) for total failure versus low rate. The authors note single-centre data and the need for external verification.
ai_technology: Bayesian network machine learning model on 24 clinical predictors
organization: Peking University; Peking University Third Hospital

evidence.tested: Tenfold cross-validation on 106,640 retrospective cycles; AUC 0.779 and 0.807.
evidence.unknown: Single centre; external verification and laboratory sperm and oocyte parameters missing; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian network learning predicted fertilization failure from patient and treatment variables.
